title: Enthusiasm: The Missing Energy of a Successful Civilization · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Modern systems can run remarkably well without anyone feeling inspired.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This essay asks why a civilization so rich in possibility struggles to commit.

direction.delivery: lift on 'struggles to commit', curious not alarmed

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its answer is enthusiasm: voluntary energy toward a future you can help shape.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Stimulation keeps nudging attention; voltage is the sense that effort moves something worthwhile.

direction.delivery: measured contrast between the two halves

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The author shows how safeguards, metrics and early evaluation make beginnings costly.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Dreams get judged as credentials or business models before they gain depth.

direction.delivery: slight weight on 'before they gain depth'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ignition needs a reachable first step, visible consequences and enough control to change the work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also confronts cults, bubbles, burnout and the unpaid passion tax.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It proposes protected experiments, honest work and communities with room for dissent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Even generative AI is weighed: who still chooses, checks and stays with the result?

direction.delivery: genuine question, rising at the end

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: If your ideas lack a credible first move, begin with “The Missing Voltage.”

direction.delivery: speak directly to the listener, short pause before the chapter title
